schema_note: Declarative self-report questionnaires. Each questionnaire has `questions` (asked in the app) and `indicators` (derived health signals the scoring engine computes from the answers). An indicator draws a numeric value either `from` one question (a number answer directly, or a choice option's `score`) or as the `sum_of` several questions (a validated instrument total), then maps it through ordered `bands` to a labelled severity (ok | watch | concern). `citation` fields ground the thresholds. Extend by adding entries here; no code change needed.

questionnaires.title: Digestive & Gut Health
questionnaires.description: A quick read on bowel regularity and stool quality — the everyday signals of gut health.

questions.text: How many bowel movements do you have in a typical week?
questions.help: Count roughly. 1 per day = 7 per week.

questions.text: Which best matches your typical stool?
How often do you strain to pass a stool?

indicators.label: Bowel regularity

bands.label: Constipated
bands.note: Fewer than 3 bowel movements per week meets the Rome IV threshold for constipation. Fibre, fluids, and movement help; persistent constipation is worth raising with a clinician.

bands.label: Low-normal
bands.note: On the low side of normal (3-4/week). More fibre and water often nudges this up.

bands.label: Frequent / loose
bands.note: More than ~3/day can signal loose stools or a GI upset if it persists.

indicators.citation: Rome IV functional constipation criteria (Lacy 2016): <3 spontaneous BM/week.

bands.label: Hard (constipation-type)
bands.note: Bristol types 1-2 are hard, slow-transit stools associated with constipation.

bands.label: Ideal
bands.note: Bristol types 3-4 are the target — well-formed and easy to pass.

bands.label: Soft
bands.note: Bristol type 5 is soft and can indicate a lack of fibre or fast transit.

bands.label: Loose (diarrhoea-type)
bands.note: Bristol types 6-7 are loose/watery; if frequent, watch hydration and see a clinician if it persists.

questionnaires.title: Hydration
questionnaires.description: Two quick signals of whether you're drinking enough day to day.

questions.text: What colour is your urine, typically, during the day?
About how many glasses of water (250 ml) do you drink per day?

indicators.label: Hydration

bands.label: Well hydrated
bands.note: Pale urine (shades 1-3) usually means you're well hydrated.

bands.label: Mildly under-hydrated
bands.note: Darker yellow suggests you could drink a bit more, especially in heat or exercise.

bands.label: Under-hydrated
bands.note: Amber/brown urine points to dehydration. Increase fluids; persistent dark urine warrants medical review.

indicators.citation: Urine colour chart validated against hydration status (Armstrong 1994).

questionnaires.title: Perceived Stress (PSS-4)
questionnaires.description: The validated 4-item Perceived Stress Scale — how uncontrollable and overloaded life has felt this past month.

questions.text: In the last month, how often have you felt unable to control the important things in your life?
In the last month, how often have you felt confident about your ability to handle your personal problems?
In the last month, how often have you felt that things were going your way?
In the last month, how often have you felt difficulties were piling up so high you could not overcome them?

bands.label: Low
bands.note: PSS-4 score in the low range — you're feeling largely in control this month.

bands.label: Moderate
bands.note: Moderate perceived stress. Recovery habits (sleep, movement, downtime) matter here.

bands.label: High
bands.note: High perceived stress. Consider active stress-reduction and support; if sustained, discuss with a clinician.
